data.reasoning: The disagreement is solely due to a transient API error in the first model (qwen) when processing the PKGBUILD, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The second model (deepseek) successfully reviewed the PKGBUILD and all other files, finding no malicious code, supply-chain attacks, or suspicious behavior. The package follows standard AUR practices, fetching from the official upstream GitLab with pinned checksums, and the build/package functions perform expected operations (including running the built binary to generate udev rules, which is a known legitimate feature of OpenRGB).
data.disagreement_analysis: Model 1 (qwen) encountered an HTTP 400 API error when auditing the PKGBUILD, forcing an inconclusive verdict. Model 2 (deepseek) successfully audited the PKGBUILD and found it safe.
coverage_issues: qwen failed to audit PKGBUILD due to an API error (HTTP 400)
learnings: Transient API errors during file review should be handled gracefully; if a secondary model successfully reviews the critical files (like PKGBUILD), the overall verdict can be resolved without requiring a full re-audit.
